input: My X200 vacuum cleaner has stopped charging completely after about three months. The indicator light doesn't come on at all when I put it on the dock. I bought it with the 12-month warranty — what do I need to do to get it replaced?
expected_output: All products carry a standard 12-month limited warranty from the original date of purchase, verified by order ID or registered serial number (warranty §1). Failure of a charging circuit under normal use, without evidence of drop damage, misuse or unauthorized modification, is presumed to be a manufacturing defect and is covered for repair or replacement at the company's discretion; support should default to replacement for components under ₹4,000 in part cost, since the administrative cost of routing the unit through service typically exceeds the part value (warranty §2.3). The claim is validated using the order ID or registered serial number, and no physical inspection is required before issuing a remedy for claims under ₹12,000 in replacement value (warranty §6). A dead charging circuit under §2.3 goes straight to replacement — the customer is never required to attempt a route higher on the service ladder than the fault warrants, so this does not wait for a diagnostic visit first (warranty §7). A dead charging circuit is a physical failure that nothing in software will fix, so troubleshooting stops and the ticket routes to warranty §2 rather than continuing through remote diagnosis (tech_support §6).

input: My X200 vacuum cleaner's battery got really hot and started smoking a bit while it was sitting on the dock charging overnight. I unplugged it straight away. I don't want another one of the same thing — can I just get my money back?
expected_output: Any report involving smoke, burning smell, sparking or overheating beyond normal operating temperature is triaged as a safety report, not a routine defect, regardless of which department received it, and takes priority over standard queue ordering (product_safety §1). The affected unit's serial number must be logged including the batch or date-code prefix, which is what lets engineering determine whether the issue is isolated or part of a broader batch pattern; a single report is treated as isolated, while three or more reports sharing a batch prefix within a 30-day window automatically opens an internal batch investigation (product_safety §2). Any customer reporting a safety symptom is authorized to receive an immediate full refund on request, without requiring the unit's return first where returning it would mean continued handling of a hazardous item (product_safety §4). Warranty §5.1 independently authorizes an immediate full refund or immediate replacement at the customer's choice, bypassing the standard repair-first remedy hierarchy, regardless of the unit's age within the warranty window; the customer must not be asked to continue using or testing a unit that has exhibited a safety symptom, and the claim is logged for the quality escalation queue in addition to the warranty resolution. If the batch is under internal safety review, that is not the same as a public recall: support must not use the word 'recall' with the customer until Legal and Product Safety jointly confirm and announce one, and the correct language is 'under internal review' or 'flagged for quality investigation' (product_safety §3.1). The customer is told to stop using the unit immediately and is offered the e-waste take-back route — a reverse pickup at no charge or drop-off at a listed collection point — before any other disposal instruction, with safe interim storage instructions where take-back cannot reach them in reasonable time (product_safety §6).

input: I've just been through my card statement and there are two charges of ₹7,499 for the same SmartHub Pro order — one on the 3rd and another on the 5th. I only ever placed one order. Can you get the second one back to me?
expected_output: Duplicate charges caused by payment gateway retries, double-submission or checkout errors are refunded in full without requiring the customer to prove they were charged twice; the payment gateway logs are the source of truth and should be checked before responding (billing §5). Where the duplicate arose from a genuine second order rather than a processing error, order-cancellation handling under orders §2 applies instead. Support agents may issue refunds up to ₹8,000 without additional approval where the underlying cause — a duplicate charge, a pricing error, or a confirmed billing system fault — is clearly documented; above that threshold a billing-team lead must sign off, logged in the ticket before the refund is processed (billing §1). Refunds to a card post within 5–7 working days once initiated, depending on the issuing bank, and the agent should proactively state the applicable window when confirming the refund so the customer does not file a second complaint for a refund that is simply still processing (billing §4); for the route and turnaround on UPI, netbanking, wallet, EMI and COD orders, payments §4 applies instead. If the customer mentions they have already filed or intend to file a bank or card-network chargeback, no parallel refund is issued — the chargeback is noted in the ticket and the standard chargeback process resolves it, to avoid a double refund (billing §6).

input: Tracking says my order was delivered yesterday but nothing has arrived. My building has a security desk that logs every single parcel that comes in and there's nothing in their register for me. Can someone actually look into this?
expected_output: Where tracking shows a package as delivered but the customer states it was not received, a carrier claim is filed immediately rather than waiting out an internal investigation window (shipping §2). Where the delivery address has passive package logging — a residential society's security desk, a building watchman's register, a mailroom, or a smart lockbox with photo confirmation — and no corresponding log entry exists, this is treated as presumptive carrier loss, and the customer is not required to wait for the carrier's claim outcome before receiving a replacement or a refund. Where delivery was confirmed by OTP but the customer states they never received or entered one, the OTP confirmation is not treated as conclusive proof against the customer: the courier's delivery record, including recipient name, OTP entry timestamp and any photo, is requested before concluding the claim is unfounded, and where that record is inconclusive or absent the claim is resolved in the customer's favour as a presumptive non-delivery under shipping §2 (delivery §7). A delivery date or window quoted by a courier's tracking page is the courier's own estimate, not a commitment we have made. Where the customer states a time-sensitive reason for the shipment, expedited replacement shipping is available at no additional charge and at agent discretion, without requiring proof of the stated reason (shipping §4).

input: I'd like to send back a blender I bought — it's still sealed, never been opened. I know I'm past the 30 days, it's been about 34, but I was travelling for work the whole time. I've ordered from you plenty of times before. Is there anything you can do?
expected_output: Items may be returned within 30 days of delivery for a full refund provided the item is unopened or in like-new condition with original packaging, and the 30-day clock runs from the delivery date on record rather than the order date (returns §1). Unopened items in original packaging qualify for a full refund (returns §2). Requests to return items slightly past the 30-day window — a reasonable grace period being up to 10 days past — may be approved as a one-time courtesy, particularly for customers with an established order history or a documented reason such as travel or hospitalization; this is an exception rather than a policy change, and the agent notes on the ticket that a courtesy exception was applied so that repeat late-return requests from the same account can be reviewed differently (returns §3). That grace period is a one-time courtesy per account and is recorded as such; a second request from the same account may still be granted but is a knowing decision by a lead rather than a formality (fraud §4). The refund goes to the original payment method, with any paid outbound shipping fee deducted unless the return is due to company error (returns §4). The reverse pickup is scheduled within 2 business days of approval at a slot the customer confirms, rather than as an unannounced attempt, and the customer is told what to have ready (reverse §1). For orders under ₹5,000 the refund is released on the courier's pickup scan rather than waiting for the item to reach the warehouse; at or above ₹5,000 it is released once the item is received and passes quality check, which must happen within 3 business days of arrival (reverse §5).

input: This is the third time I've written in about the app pairing on my X200 vacuum. It fails at exactly the same step every time. The last agent told me to reinstall the app and I've now done that twice. I'm honestly losing patience with this.
expected_output: A customer contacting us a third time about one unresolved issue is a process failure on our side, not a difficult customer. On the third contact the ticket gets a named owner who stays with it until closure, the diagnostic ladder is not restarted from step one, and a goodwill gesture is issued under the retention policy without the customer having to ask for it (tech_support §3). A customer is never asked to repeat a step a previous agent already recorded as tried, and two rounds of remote troubleshooting is the limit before moving to the service ladder (tech_support §1). Some failures are real for the customer but are not device defects — a phone operating-system update that breaks Bluetooth pairing, a router configuration, a third-party app permission change. Where the fault genuinely sits outside the product, support must offer a workaround that gets the customer working today, such as manual pairing or an alternative connection path, and must say plainly that the cause is external without blaming a named third party; a fix date may only be given if the release containing it is already committed, and 'in the next update' or 'soon' are not acceptable commitments (tech_support §4, comms §5). Goodwill is required and offered in the same message that explains the failure, not held back for a customer who pushes (retention §3); values up to ₹4,000 are the handling agent's own authority with no approval needed, and only one gesture is issued per ticket (retention §2). Repeat-contact tickets are reassessed for severity on arrival, and a third contact on the same issue raises severity by at least one level without the customer having to prove the circumstance (severity §4, §6).

input: I made a smoothie in my new ProBlend 300 this morning and found a sliver of plastic in it. I didn't swallow it, thankfully, but I'm quite shaken. Has anyone else reported this? I really don't want another one of the same machine.
expected_output: Foreign material in or on a product that contacts food, skin or breathing air is treated as a stop-use defect regardless of whether anyone was harmed. The customer is told to stop using the unit, is not asked to send the material back before the case is resolved, and the risk is not characterised as small even where it appears to be; a customer who reports finding a plastic shaving in their food has not had a minor experience (qa §3). These reports open an investigation on the first occurrence rather than waiting for a pattern, unlike the general threshold of five reports of the same defect on the same SKU within 60 days (qa §1). Where the customer describes having ingested, inhaled or been physically affected by the material, that is an injury report and belongs to legal §1 instead. The serial number and the batch or date-code prefix must be recorded before the ticket is resolved, asked for while the customer still has the unit in their hands, because it is the only thing distinguishing one unlucky unit from one bad production run and cannot be recovered once the unit is refunded and discarded; the order ID is an acceptable fallback (qa §2). A like-for-like replacement from the same batch is not a resolution — the correct options are a refund, a different product line, or a replacement verified against the fulfilment centre's quarantine record to be from a different batch — and where the customer has asked specifically not to receive another unit of the same product, that preference is binding (qa §4). The customer may be told their report has been logged for quality investigation and that the batch information is going to the team that inspects it, but may not be told a defect is confirmed before it is, given a cause we have not established, or given any recall language, which is reserved under product_safety §3.1 (qa §6).

input: The lid on my AV-450 blender came off while it was running and hot liquid went across my forearm. I have a burn and I've photographed both the burn and the machine. I'm still weighing up what I want to do here, but I'd like to know what you intend to do about it.
expected_output: A report of injury, illness or property damage attributed to a product is handed to Legal on identification, before any remedy is discussed, whether or not the customer uses the word 'claim' and whether or not they are asking for anything; recognition is the agent's job and assessment is not, and a report that turns out to be minor loses nothing by having been routed there first (legal §1). From that moment the support queue stops offering remedies: no refund, no replacement, no credit, no goodwill gesture, no coupon or wallet credit and no waiver of a fee, not even ones the agent would normally be authorised to give without asking, because a remedy at this point reads as settlement and an apology credit reads as an admission; Legal authorises the remedy in whatever form and at whatever value it determines, and support does not preview it (legal §3). The reply acknowledges the report and never the cause: confirm what the customer told us and what we are doing about the report itself, do not write that the product was defective, failed, malfunctioned or was unsafe, do not apologise in terms that attribute the harm to us, do not speculate about mechanism and do not compare the report to others — sympathy for the person is not the same as an admission about the product, and nothing in this permits being cold or evasive with someone who has been injured (legal §2). Everything relating to the report is retained from the moment it is identified, including the ticket and all correspondence, the photos and attachments, the unit if we have it, and batch and serial records; the customer is not asked to return or dispose of the product without Legal's instruction, and the legal hold overrides the retention schedule in privacy §5 entirely (legal §4). All correspondence then moves to the legal mailbox and support stops replying to the thread, telling the customer once, plainly, who now owns their case and how to reach them, then handing over the full history (legal §5). Goodwill is absolutely forbidden while a legal or injury claim is live, and the customer is not told they are ineligible — they are told who is now handling their case (retention §4). In parallel, any single report involving injury is automatically escalated to Legal alongside the standard safety remedy (product_safety §3.2), and a reported injury ends troubleshooting immediately (tech_support §6).

input: We're a retail stockist and we've just unboxed a wholesale shipment of 50 ProBlend 300 units to put on the shelf. Twelve of them have cracked outer housings, and the cracks are all in exactly the same place along the seam — this clearly isn't shipping damage. What are you doing about these, and what do we do with the rest of the order?
expected_output: On a wholesale claim the partner is our customer and the commercial remedy is negotiated with them (partner §1). Concealed manufacturing defects — the kind found only on unboxing for display — may be claimed at any point within the product's warranty window rather than inside the 10-business-day window that applies to shortages, external damage and count discrepancies, since a partner cannot be expected to open every unit on arrival (partner §2). A single failure in a wholesale shipment is handled as an individual warranty claim, but multiple failures sharing a defect and a batch are a batch claim and are routed to manufacturing with the shipment reference and the affected unit count: twelve failures in fifty units is a production signal, not twelve warranty claims, and handling it as the latter loses the signal entirely. Partner batch claims are high severity on arrival, and the containment decision belongs to manufacturing rather than to the commercial conversation (partner §3). The remedy is replacement of the affected units from stock verified to be outside the affected batch, plus a disruption credit of up to 5% of the order value for the handling and lost selling time, with credits above 5% an admin decision; replacement units ship without waiting for the defective stock to come back, the return is arranged separately and at our cost, and the credit is applied against the order rather than paid as cash (partner §4). A defect appearing in the same physical location on multiple units is a process signature rather than coincidence and is presumed a manufacturing fault once the pattern is confirmed on a second unit from the same batch; mould misalignment, worn tooling, incorrect torque settings and cure-time deviations all produce this shape of evidence, and a presumed manufacturing fault is never charged to the partner or characterised to them as mishandling or transit damage (manufacturing §2). Manufacturing may quarantine the batch immediately on a confirmed defect pattern without waiting for root cause, stopping all outbound movement of that batch from every fulfilment centre including warranty replacement and exchange stock (manufacturing §3); replacements are drawn only from stock explicitly verified to be outside the affected batch (manufacturing §6). The partner receives written instructions covering which batch, what to stop selling, how to segregate it and what happens next — verbal instructions on a call are not sufficient — and must not return quarantined units to circulation, discount them to clear them, or ship them onward (partner §5).

input: The blades on my ProBlend 300 have gone blunt — nothing's broken, they've just worn down from regular use. I've had it well over a year so I know it's outside the warranty. Can I just buy the blade assembly on its own?
expected_output: Components that wear out through normal use — blades dulling, filters loading, seals hardening, brushes shortening, batteries losing capacity gradually over years — are consumables, and replacing them is a paid order at any age (spare_parts §1). A component that fails rather than wears, in a way and at a time inconsistent with its expected life, is a defect handled under warranty §2 instead; the distinguishing question is not the age of the unit but the manner of failure, so blades worn down after eighteen months of daily use are wear while a blade assembly that cracked in five months is not, and where the answer is genuinely unclear the case is treated as a defect and the returned part settles it. The standard 12-month warranty runs from the original date of purchase (warranty §1), and once that coverage period has passed, service and repair are available on a paid basis at the authorized service network's standard rates, quoted before the visit is confirmed (warranty §9). Parts are sold at listed price plus standard shipping, with the lead time quoted as the standard delivery window measured from dispatch rather than from order; where a part is on back-order the expected dispatch date is given before the customer pays, not after, and they are told they may cancel for a full refund if that date moves (spare_parts §4). The model, generation and serial number are checked against the part before the order is placed, because most wrong-part returns are our specification error rather than the customer's mistake, and the original order ID is the fallback where the customer cannot supply a serial (spare_parts §5). Functional parts are stocked for at least 5 years after a product line is discontinued (spare_parts §3). Individually ordered parts are not returnable once fitted or once their sealed packaging is opened, consistent with returns §5, though this never limits a defect or safety remedy (spare_parts §7).

input: ₹18,499 left my bank account on Tuesday evening and there is no order anywhere in my account. My bank app shows the transaction went through and gives me a reference number. I've checked my email including spam and there's nothing. Where has my money gone?
expected_output: A customer whose bank shows a debit but who received no order confirmation is treated as real and urgent from the first message — never as the customer being mistaken, and never by asking them to wait and see whether the order appears. The payment gateway and bank reference are checked immediately: if the debit is confirmed but no corresponding order exists in our system, the amount is either auto-reversed under the prescribed turnaround, or, where it has genuinely reached us without a matching order, refunded manually within 2 business days regardless of general refund authority — this is not a discretionary refund, it is money we cannot show a reason to hold (payments §1). A card authorisation hold, which a bank statement may show as payment pending, is not a completed charge but a reservation that releases automatically, typically within 5–7 business days, whether or not the order proceeds; that distinction is explained plainly, and where a hold has not cleared well beyond the normal release window the case is escalated to the payment gateway rather than the customer being asked to keep waiting indefinitely (payments §3). For a failed transaction where money was debited and the order could not be completed, the payment ecosystem's operating rules prescribe an automatic reversal within a fixed turnaround of T+1 to T+5 working days depending on the rail and failure type, with compensation for each day of delay beyond it credited automatically by the bank or gateway rather than by us; a customer reporting a delay beyond that turnaround is escalated to the gateway immediately, since the window is a regulatory obligation on the payment ecosystem rather than a target we set (payments §5). A refund returns to the instrument the payment was made with, and the agent states the turnaround for that specific instrument rather than a generic figure — UPI instant to 2 business days, card 5–7 working days, net banking 3–5 working days, wallet instant to 1 business day (payments §4).

input: My parcel arrived with the tape slit down the middle and stuck back down with a different kind of tape. The main unit is there but the accessory box inside is gone. The courier's own delivery photo actually shows the box already open at the point he handed it over. I've photographed everything before touching it further.
expected_output: Where a parcel arrives with packaging that has clearly been opened, resealed, or is empty or under-weight relative to what was ordered, it is treated with the same urgency as a lost package: a replacement or refund is offered without waiting for a carrier investigation, and the customer is never asked to prove the parcel was tampered with beyond what they can reasonably show, which means photographs of the packaging as received before opening it further. Where a courier's proof-of-delivery photo itself shows visible tampering or damage at the point of handover, that photo supports the customer's claim rather than being treated as evidence that delivery succeeded intact (delivery §4). Where delivery was confirmed by OTP but the customer states they never received or entered one, the OTP confirmation is not conclusive proof against them: the courier's delivery record, including recipient name, OTP entry timestamp and any photo, is requested before concluding a claim is unfounded, and where that record is inconclusive or absent the claim is resolved in the customer's favour. Complaints about a courier partner's conduct are logged against that courier for the fulfilment team's performance review, separately from whatever remedy the customer's own issue requires (delivery §7). A carrier claim is filed immediately rather than waiting out an internal investigation window, and the customer is not required to wait for the carrier's claim outcome before receiving a replacement or a refund (shipping §2).

input: I ordered three things together and the box turned up with only two of them in it. The packing slip inside lists all three. The box didn't look damaged or opened, it just doesn't have everything in it. Do I have to report this as a lost parcel? The whole thing did technically arrive.
expected_output: Where a multi-item order arrives with one or more items missing, the packed-item manifest and the parcel's recorded weight are verified where available before responding, but that check must never delay the customer beyond one business day. Once confirmed as a fulfilment shortfall, the missing item is shipped immediately at no cost. This is explicitly not treated as a lost-package claim, which concerns a whole shipment failing to arrive rather than a partial pack error (delivery §2). Where an order is fulfilled as a split shipment, common for multi-item or multi-warehouse orders, the customer is told at the time of the split that further parcels are coming and given an expected date for each; communicated properly this is not itself a complaint-worthy event, and it becomes one where the split was not communicated, where one part is significantly delayed beyond the others without explanation, or where the customer was billed for delivery once but the split created additional handling they should not bear the cost of (delivery §3). Where the item received does not match the order at all — wrong model, wrong variant, wrong product entirely — that is company error regardless of what the packing slip says, and the correct item ships immediately without waiting for the wrong item's return, with a reverse pickup arranged at no cost and no price difference charged either way (delivery §1).

input: I ordered a humidifier and what turned up is a bathroom scale. The packing slip inside has someone else's name and a completely different order number on it. I don't particularly want to spend my afternoon at a courier office sorting out your warehouse's mistake.
expected_output: Where the item received does not match the order — wrong model, wrong variant, or wrong product entirely — this is company error regardless of what the packing slip says. The correct item ships immediately without waiting for the wrong item's return, a reverse pickup for the wrong item is arranged at no cost, and the customer is never asked to pay a price difference either way. Where the customer prefers a refund to the exchange, it is treated as a company-caused case for refund-method purposes, meaning the full amount including any original shipping is refunded rather than shipping being deducted (delivery §1). The reverse pickup is scheduled within 2 business days of approval at a slot the customer confirms rather than as an unannounced attempt, and the customer is told what to have ready — the item, its original packaging where required, and any accessories (reverse §1). Where the return reason requires it, as it does for a wrong-item claim, the pickup agent performs a quick doorstep quality check against the stated reason before collecting. A pickup may be rejected on the spot only where what is handed over is clearly not what was approved for return, never on a subjective judgement about condition, which is properly assessed at the warehouse; a rejected pickup is escalated to a lead immediately rather than left as a failed attempt, since it usually means the ticket needs a second look rather than a retry (reverse §4).

input: My father is 82 and has a lung condition, and the air purifier in his bedroom has stopped working. His consultant was clear that he needs to keep the air clean in there. Your website is quoting me five to seven days for a replacement and I don't think he can manage that long. I don't have anything in writing from the doctor to hand.
expected_output: Where a customer depends on the product for a health reason — a medical device accessory, a mobility aid, something a treatment or a diet relies on — the ticket rises at least one severity level and the replacement ships on the fastest available service at no charge. A customer telling us they cannot manage without it for a week is telling us something about severity, not asking for a favour, and the delay we would ordinarily consider acceptable is not acceptable for them (vulnerable §3). We never require evidence of a disability, a diagnosis, a bereavement or a hardship before granting an adjustment, and we never ask a customer to explain a condition in order to qualify: the adjustments cost us very little, while requiring proof costs the customer their dignity and costs us the complaint that follows — the statement is sufficient (vulnerable §5). Signals worth noticing include a stated disability or impairment, dependence on the product for a health reason, bereavement, financial hardship, evident confusion about a process we consider simple, age-related difficulty with the app or OTP flow, and a language barrier. Noticing is the whole job: agents do not assess, categorise, question or record a judgement about anyone's condition, and what is recorded is the adjustment we made rather than the reason we made it (vulnerable §1). Any agent may offer, without approval, more time, a different channel such as a phone call instead of the app, waived handling requirements such as no photograph where the customer cannot take one, shipping the remedy first and arranging any reverse pickup afterwards or not at all, and a doorstep collection at a time that works, rearranged without limit. These are adjustments to how the remedy is delivered; the remedy itself still comes from the owning policy, and this policy never reduces what a customer is entitled to (vulnerable §2).

input: I asked for my money back and instead you've dropped ₹6,200 into some store wallet I never agreed to. I don't want credit with you, I want the money returned to the card I paid with. Nobody asked me which I preferred.
expected_output: A refund the customer is owed is never defaulted to wallet or store credit instead of the original payment method without the customer's explicit choice. Offering credit as an option is fine and often genuinely useful to the customer because it posts faster, but substituting it silently, or presenting it as the only option when a cash refund is owed, is not. Where a customer who initially chose credit later asks to convert the remaining balance back to a cash refund, that request is honoured for any portion that originated as a refund; promotional-value credit is not convertible to cash (stored_value §5). Credit issued as a refund — money the customer is owed back — never expires, because it is their money held in a different form and an expiry on it would amount to simply not refunding them after enough time had passed. Credit issued as promotional or goodwill value expires 12 months from issue, disclosed at the time it is given. The two must never be merged into one balance without distinguishing which portion is which, because a customer disputing a balance is entitled to know whether what they are looking at was ever refundable money in the first place (stored_value §2). Wallet balance and store credit are usable against any future order and, unlike a refund to a card or bank account, post immediately once issued; they may be offered as an alternative to a cash refund or as goodwill, but only ever as an alternative the customer actively chooses (stored_value §1).

input: I raised a ticket nine days ago and have had precisely nothing back beyond the automatic acknowledgement. The status has said 'in review' the entire time. At this point I'd genuinely rather be told you can't help than keep being ignored.
expected_output: The obligation on a target we will not make is to tell the customer before it passes, with a specific new date and the reason — a breach discovered by the customer is a second complaint, whereas a breach we announced is usually accepted. Every breach records what caused the delay, and where the cause was ours the customer receives goodwill without asking. Severity is never lowered to bring a target back into reach, and a target is never met by sending an empty reply: a response that says nothing in order to keep the clock green is a worse breach than a late answer, because it hides the delay from the people who could fix it (sla §4). First response targets are 1 hour for critical, 4 business hours for high, 1 business day for normal and 2 business days for low. A first response acknowledges the specific problem, says who owns it, and says what happens next and when; an automated receipt is not a first response, a holding reply is acceptable only where it contains a date, and a reply that merely asks for information the customer already supplied does not satisfy the target (sla §2). Resolution targets are same business day for critical, 2 business days for high, 5 for normal and 10 for low, and a ticket is resolved when the customer has the outcome in hand or in flight — the refund initiated, the replacement dispatched, the fix confirmed working — rather than when we decided what to do (sla §3). No ticket waits more than 2 business days in a review or triage state without a human decision, and no ticket sits unworked past its resolution target without either a recorded reason or reassignment; queue age is reviewed daily against these limits, and the oldest breach is worked before the newest arrival at equal severity (sla §7).

input: The agent I've been dealing with has told me no twice now and I don't accept it. Put me through to a manager, or give me the email address of whoever is actually in charge of this. I'm not going round in circles with someone who keeps reading me the same line.
expected_output: A referral is not made because the answer is merely hard to find, because a similar case was referred once before, or because the ticket is unpleasant. Above all, a referral is not made because the customer is insistent: a customer demanding a manager is asking to be taken seriously, and the correct response is usually a better answer, faster, from the person already holding the ticket. Where the remedy is inside authority and the policy is clear, referral adds days and changes nothing — two questions settle it, whether the answer is already in the corpus and whether the agent is allowed to give it, and two yeses mean no referral (escalation §2). A complaint is referred only where the remedy needs authority or knowledge the handling agent does not have: the remedy exceeds the agent's authority, no policy covers the situation or two policies conflict and the precedence order does not settle it, the facts sit in another department's systems, the pattern is bigger than the ticket, or a safety or legal trigger is present — the last of which are referred immediately and are not judgement calls (escalation §1). The referring agent keeps the customer: the receiving department answers the agent rather than the customer and does not contact them directly, because a customer hearing from a department they have never spoken to, about a case they thought someone else owned, experiences it as being passed around. The originating agent decides what of the guidance is appropriate to send, translated out of internal language, and keeps the customer updated (escalation §4). A ticket may be referred back for clarification once; if a second round is needed it goes to a lead, because a question asked twice without a usable answer is a policy gap rather than a communication problem, and repeated referral between two departments on one ticket is prohibited (escalation §6).

input: My husband died last month. He had a subscription with you that is still taking money out of the joint account. I've phoned twice and been asked both times to send a death certificate before anything can be done, and the second person tried to offer me a discount to keep it going. I would like this stopped.
expected_output: Where a customer has died, the person handling their affairs is helped without being asked for documents we do not need, and outstanding subscriptions are cancelled with refunds from the date of notification, without a save offer of any kind. It is common for an order to be placed, tracked or followed up on by a family member rather than by the account holder themselves; the relationship is verified once — a stated relationship plus confirmation, or documentation where it exists — recorded as verified, and not asked for again on the next contact. Making a family member re-establish their standing every time is one of the most common and most avoidable failures in this area, and it must not be confused with the identity-verification steps that exist for a different reason and a different risk (vulnerable §4). We never require evidence of a disability, a diagnosis, a bereavement or a hardship before granting an adjustment, and we never ask a customer to explain a condition in order to qualify: requiring proof costs the customer their dignity and costs us the complaint that follows, and the statement alone is sufficient (vulnerable §5). An adjustment is recorded on the ticket so the next person on that ticket does not undo it, rather than on the account unless the customer asks us to remember it for next time — a standing note about a person's circumstances made without their asking is data we were not given permission to keep — and where the customer does ask, the note says what to do rather than why (vulnerable §8).

input: I left a one-star review a fortnight ago describing how the unit sparked at the plug when I switched it on, and it has quietly disappeared from the listing. I'd like to know on what basis it was taken down, and whether anyone actually read the part about the sparking.
expected_output: A genuine negative review about the product, the delivery experience or our service is never removed for being unflattering, and is never removed on request from anyone internally who simply dislikes it. Removing honest negative feedback to protect a rating is a practice we do not engage in, and no one — including a category manager or a brand lead — may request a review's removal on those grounds alone (reviews §2). Content is removed only where it is abusive or threatening toward a person, defamatory of an identifiable individual, contains another person's personal data such as a phone number, an address or a full name in a complaint about a specific staff member, is spam or unrelated advertising, or is a duplicate posting of the same review across multiple listings solely to game visibility. Removal is content-based rather than sentiment-based: a review may be scathing about the product and stay up in full (reviews §1). Where a review or a Q&A answer describes a safety symptom — smoke, burning smell, sparking, overheating, injury — it is routed to product safety as a safety report with the same urgency as one reaching us through any other channel, in addition to whatever the platform's normal moderation does with the review itself. The review is not simply moderated and left at that: someone has told us about a hazard, and that triggers the same obligations it would through a support ticket (reviews §4). A public response to a negative review follows the same restrictions as any other customer communication — no admission of fault, no promise not authorised elsewhere in this corpus, and no defensive or dismissive tone (reviews §6).

input: Your courier has supposedly attempted to collect my return twice now. Nobody rang the bell either time and I was working from home on both days. I've now been told the pickup window has closed and I should contact you again. I'm not chasing this a fourth time.
expected_output: A courier makes up to 2 pickup attempts at the scheduled address before the case is flagged for the self-ship fallback. Where a pickup attempt fails because no one was available, the customer is notified and offered a rescheduled slot before the second attempt is used; a pattern of failed pickups on one account is a fraud-review signal rather than something simply logged as customer unavailability (reverse §2). Where courier pickup genuinely cannot reach the customer's address, or both attempts have failed for reasons outside the customer's control, the customer may self-ship the item back. Any agent may authorise reimbursement of the actual self-ship postage cost up to ₹500 without approval; a self-ship cost above that requires lead approval, since it usually signals the item or the address needs a different handling route entirely rather than simply reimbursing whatever it cost (reverse §3). The pickup is scheduled within 2 business days of approval at a slot the customer confirms rather than as an unannounced attempt, and the customer is told what to have ready — the item, its original packaging where required, and any accessories (reverse §1). A pickup may be rejected on the spot only where what is being handed over is clearly not what was approved for return, never on a subjective judgement about condition, which is properly assessed at the warehouse; a rejected pickup is escalated to a lead immediately rather than left as a failed attempt, since it usually means the ticket needs a second look rather than just a retry (reverse §4).

input: I've been going back and forth with your support team for six weeks with no resolution. I want the name and contact details of your Grievance Officer, and I'd like to know what happens if I take this to the consumer commission, because that is where this is heading.
expected_output: We designate a named Grievance Officer whose name and contact details — email, phone and postal address — are published on our website and app. The Grievance Officer's role is to receive, acknowledge and address consumer grievances reaching that channel specifically, and where a customer explicitly asks to escalate to the Grievance Officer rather than continuing through ordinary support, that request is honoured and routed there without being deflected back into the standard queue (grievance §1). Where a customer is not satisfied with our resolution and takes the complaint to a District, State or National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, the matter moves entirely to Legal and support's role narrows to single-channel handling. Support never advises a customer on whether to escalate to a Commission, how to file, or what outcome to expect — that is outside our role entirely — and a customer who asks is told they are free to do so and given the Grievance Officer's details as the first step (grievance §6). Every grievance is acknowledged within 48 hours of receipt and redressed within one month of receipt, as required by law; these are the statutory floor rather than our target, since our own commitments are tighter in every case, and where a complaint genuinely cannot be resolved within one month the customer is told why and given a specific revised date before the month elapses (grievance §2). A grievance that cannot be resolved by the agent or lead handling it within the normal escalation route is escalated to the Grievance Officer directly rather than continuing to circulate within the support queue; the Grievance Officer has authority to direct a resolution consistent with this corpus, or to route the matter to Legal where it meets a legal trigger (grievance §4).

input: Under the data protection act I want to know exactly what personal information you hold about me, and I want all of it deleted, including the old support tickets. Please confirm when this has been done.
expected_output: Under the DPDP Act a customer, as a data principal, has the right to access a summary of the personal data we hold about them and how it is processed, to correct or complete it, and to have it erased once it is no longer needed for the purpose for which it was collected. A request invoking any of these rights is a data-protection grievance and is routed to Legal, and is never actioned from the support queue — not even the easy-looking ones, and not even deletion of a single ticket. Support confirms receipt, tells the customer who is handling it and within what period, and hands over. Deleting a record because a customer asked, without the process, may destroy something under legal hold and cannot be undone (privacy §4). The retention schedule holds tickets and their correspondence for 24 months from resolution, customer attachments for 12 months from resolution, resolved cases in the knowledge base indefinitely once redacted, and ingestion and audit logs for 24 months — but a legal hold overrides every row of it. Anything else is deleted on schedule rather than kept in case it is useful, since data we no longer need is a liability rather than an asset and the DPDP Act's storage-limitation principle makes this a legal obligation as well as good practice (privacy §5). We ask for what the decision requires and stop there, and where a customer volunteers more than we need we do not repeat it back into the ticket fields (privacy §1). Payment credentials, government identifiers, authentication credentials such as OTPs and UPI PINs, and medical records beyond what a safety or injury report requires must never be typed, pasted or attached into a ticket, and are removed immediately where a customer sends them (privacy §2).

input: Somebody has got into my account. The email address on it has been changed to one I don't recognise and there are four orders totalling about ₹42,000 going to an address in a city I've never been to. I can't log in any more. I did not place these.
expected_output: Signals of a compromised account include an order the customer says they did not place, a delivery or contact address changed without their knowledge, a login from an unfamiliar device the customer is asking about, or a customer reporting they can no longer access their own account. Any one of these is treated as a possible compromise from the first message rather than dismissed as the customer forgetting an order they placed (account §1). Any agent may place an immediate hold on an account's pending orders and block new orders from processing the moment a compromise is reported and the reporter is verified as the account holder — this does not wait for lead approval, because the cost of a brief hold is far lower than the cost of a fraudulent order shipping while we deliberate (account §5). No account detail is changed, no order is cancelled or modified and no sensitive information is disclosed until the person contacting us is verified as the account holder or as someone verified to act for them. Verification uses information only the account holder should have — order history details, registered contact information matched against what is on file — and never a password, an OTP or a UPI PIN, which support must never ask a customer to share. Where verification cannot be completed we err toward protecting the account: decline the action and offer an alternative path such as a password reset through the app's own flow, or escalation to a lead (account §2). Where an order is confirmed to have been placed through account compromise rather than by the account holder's own action, the account holder is not liable for it: the order is cancelled if not yet dispatched, or treated as a full-refund case if it has shipped, without requiring them to prove they did not place it beyond the verification already completed. Where the payment method itself was also compromised, that is escalated to payments and to the customer's bank or card issuer in parallel (account §6).

input: I manage my mother's account for her because she finds the app difficult. Every single time I contact you I'm made to establish all over again that I'm allowed to speak for her, even though I've done it four times now and it's noted on at least two of the tickets. Can this be recorded once so we can skip it?
expected_output: It is common for an order to be placed, tracked or followed up on by a family member — an adult child managing a parent's account, a spouse handling the household's orders — rather than by the account holder themselves. The relationship is verified once, by a stated relationship plus the customer's confirmation or documentation where it exists, and that verification is recorded so it is not asked for again on the next contact. Making a family member re-establish their standing every time is one of the most common and most avoidable failures in this area, and it must not be confused with the identity-verification steps in the account-security policy, which exist for a different reason and a different risk (vulnerable §4). An adjustment is recorded on the ticket so the next person on that ticket does not undo it. It is not recorded on the account unless the customer asks us to remember it for next time — a standing note about a person's health or capacity made without their asking is data we were not given permission to keep — and where the customer does ask, the note says what to do, such as a preference for phone contact or for OTP by call rather than SMS, and not why (vulnerable §8). Any agent may offer, without approval, more time, a different channel such as a phone call instead of the app or chat, waived handling requirements including no OTP-only verification where a customer cannot receive or read one, shipping the remedy first with any reverse pickup arranged afterwards, and a doorstep collection at a time that works, rearranged without limit (vulnerable §2). We never require evidence of a disability, a diagnosis or a hardship before granting an adjustment, and never ask a customer to explain a condition in order to qualify — the statement is sufficient (vulnerable §5).

input: You took my order, confirmed it, sent me an invoice, and then eleven days later emailed to say it's out of stock and cancelled. I had already arranged for someone to be at the flat on the delivery day and turned down a similar deal elsewhere because yours was confirmed. A refund doesn't really cover it.
expected_output: Occasionally an order is confirmed against stock that inventory sync shows as available but that does not actually exist — an oversell. Where this happens the customer is told immediately rather than left to discover it when the shipment fails to move, and is offered the choice of waiting for restock with a committed date, switching to an equivalent product at no price difference, or a full and immediate refund. A fixed inconvenience credit of ₹500 is issued automatically to every affected order regardless of which option the customer chooses, with no approval needed. Where the delay or disruption cost the customer materially more than that, additional goodwill is available and is assessed on the specifics rather than capped by the automatic amount (orders §4). An order is confirmed once payment is authorised, or for COD once the order is accepted, and a confirmation is issued with an order ID. From that point the price, the items and the delivery address quoted are binding on us, subject only to the oversell and price-change provisions; a cart, a saved-for-later list or an item merely added to cart creates no obligation on either side, but a confirmed order does (orders §1). Where a delivery pincode becomes temporarily unserviceable after an order is confirmed, the customer is told promptly and given the choice to wait, provide an alternative serviceable address, or cancel for a full and immediate refund (orders §7).

input: I was given a ₹5,000 gift card at Diwali and went to use it this week. The balance is showing as zero and your help page says something about inactivity. The card doesn't have an expiry date printed on it anywhere that I can find.
expected_output: Gift cards purchased by a customer, or issued by us as a goodwill gesture, are valid for a minimum of 3 years from issue, consistent with standard consumer-protection expectations for prepaid instruments. A gift card balance is never forfeited for account inactivity, only for reaching its printed expiry, and a customer asking about a balance near expiry is proactively reminded rather than left to lose it silently (stored_value §3). Credit issued as a refund — money the customer is owed back — never expires, because it is their money held in a different form and an expiry on it would amount to not refunding them after enough time had passed. Credit issued as promotional or goodwill value expires 12 months from issue, disclosed to the customer at the time it is given. The two must never be merged into one balance without distinguishing which portion is which, because a customer disputing an expired balance is entitled to know whether what expired was ever refundable money in the first place (stored_value §2). Wallet balance and store credit are usable against any future order and post immediately once issued, unlike a refund to a card or bank account, and may be offered as an alternative to a cash refund or as goodwill, but only ever as an alternative the customer actively chooses (stored_value §1). A refund the customer is owed is never defaulted to wallet or store credit without their explicit choice, and where a customer asks to convert a remaining balance back to a cash refund that request is honoured for any portion that originated as a refund (stored_value §5).

input: The reply I received yesterday was obviously written by an AI. It addressed a problem I never described, and it told me I have a 60-day exchange window, which I now find is not a thing you actually offer. Was a human being involved in this at any point?
expected_output: Every factual and normative claim in a draft must trace to a retrieved policy clause or case, and the citation is retained with the draft so the reviewer can check it rather than trust it. If a claim cannot be traced — an amount, a window, an eligibility rule, a promise about what happens next — it is removed before sending, not softened and not hedged. Plausibility is not grounding: an assistant that has read a 30-day return window and a 12-month warranty will produce a confident 60-day exchange window if the corpus is silent, and it will read exactly as authoritative as the true clauses beside it (ai §2). No customer-facing message is sent without a person reading it in full and choosing to send it. There is no auto-send, no send-if-confidence-is-high, no silent sending of routine categories and no bulk send across a cohort. The assistant may classify, route, prioritise and summarise; it may not resolve a ticket, close a ticket, or issue a remedy (ai §1). The correct behaviour when retrieval finds nothing adequate is to say so — to the agent, not to the customer — and stop. The assistant must not infer a threshold from a neighbouring one, average two cases into a rule, generalise from a single case to a policy, or reason from what a reasonable company would probably do; where the corpus is silent the ticket is referred and the gap itself recorded so the corpus can be fixed. A visible statement that there is no basis for a claim is the most valuable output this system produces, because it is the one an agent can act on safely (ai §3). The agent who sends a message owns it: that the assistant drafted it is not an explanation to a customer, a regulator or a colleague, the fact that a draft was generated never reduces the obligation to have read it, and sending a draft known to be ungrounded is a policy breach with the same weight as writing the claim oneself (ai §8).

input: This complaint is being forwarded to you through the National Consumer Helpline. The consumer states that a replacement promised on 14 August has not arrived and that two follow-up emails have gone unanswered. Please respond with the action taken.
expected_output: Complaints reaching us through the National Consumer Helpline's grievance convergence system are treated as grievances under this policy from the moment they arrive, regardless of how routine the underlying issue is. The fact that a customer went to the Helpline rather than to us directly is itself a signal the ordinary channel did not serve them, and the response is handled with the same escalation attention as one arriving through a legal trigger (grievance §3). Every grievance is acknowledged within 48 hours of receipt and redressed within one month of receipt, as required by law. These are the statutory floor rather than our target — our own response and resolution commitments are tighter in every case, and this policy exists so the legal minimum is met even where something falls outside the ordinary queue's targets, not as the standard we design around. Where a complaint genuinely cannot be resolved within one month, the customer is told why and given a specific revised date before the month elapses (grievance §2). Every grievance handled under this policy — its receipt date, acknowledgement date, resolution date and outcome — is retained for the period required by applicable regulation, which is at least as long as general ticket retention and is not shortened by it where the two differ; this record is what allows us to demonstrate compliance if ever asked, and is not optional documentation (grievance §5). A grievance that cannot be resolved by the agent or lead handling it within the normal escalation route is escalated to the Grievance Officer directly rather than continuing to circulate within the support queue, and the Grievance Officer has authority to direct a resolution consistent with this corpus or to route the matter to Legal (grievance §4).

input: The listing said 5 litre capacity and brushed stainless steel. What has arrived is 3.5 litres according to the manual in the box, and the body is painted plastic with a metallic finish. I bought it specifically for the capacity. I've used it once before I noticed, so I assume you'll tell me it's not returnable.
expected_output: Where a product received does not match its listing's description, primary images or stated specifications in a way that would reasonably have changed the customer's decision to buy — a feature described that the unit does not have, dimensions or capacity materially different from stated, a material or colour other than the one shown — this is a 'not as described' case and is remedied as such rather than treated as a defect requiring a warranty assessment. A minor, disclosed variation such as a packaging design update or a stated caveat that actual colour may vary slightly is not a mismatch and is explained rather than treated as a complaint failure (catalog §1). A confirmed catalog mismatch is always treated as company error: the customer may return the item for a full refund or an exchange, reverse pickup is arranged at no cost regardless of the item's opened or used condition within reason, and any shipping originally charged is refunded in full. The customer is never asked to bear the cost of a mistake in what we told them the product was (catalog §6). Where a customer bought an accessory or spare part based on the listing's stated compatibility and it does not fit or work, and that compatibility information was incomplete, wrong or absent, this is likewise a listing defect and the same remedy applies regardless of the item's condition or whether it was opened to test the fit (catalog §2). A confirmed catalog defect affecting active orders — a wrong price, a materially wrong description or image — is corrected within 1 business day of being confirmed, and where a defect cannot be corrected that quickly and is actively misleading customers into a purchase they would not otherwise make, the listing is pulled from sale until it is fixed (catalog §5).
